title: Cluster API and CAPO
description: Cluster API (core, kubeadm bootstrap and control plane), CAPO and ORC on a Cluster API management cluster (test-capi or prod-capi): workload cluster state, OpenStack API calls and controller health.

panels.title: Workload clusters
panels.description: Cluster API Cluster objects on the selected management cluster (one per magnum COE cluster).

panels.title: Clusters not Available
panels.description: Clusters whose v1beta2 Available condition is False.

panels.title: Clusters not Provisioned
panels.description: Clusters in any phase other than Provisioned (Pending, Provisioning, Deleting, Failed, Unknown). Expected briefly during create and delete.

panels.title: Machines
panels.description: All Machines (control plane and workers) across workload clusters.

panels.title: Machines not Running
panels.description: Machines in any phase other than Running. Expected briefly during scale and rollout.

panels.title: Cluster cache disconnected
panels.description: Workload clusters that at least one CAPI controller cannot reach through its cluster cache (the management cluster's connection to the workload cluster's API server).

panels.title: Controller targets down
panels.description: Metrics endpoints of the CAPI, CAPO and ORC controllers that Prometheus cannot scrape.

panels.title: Controllers without a leader
panels.description: Controller deployments with no pod holding the leader lease. A controller without a leader does no work.

targets.expr: count(count by (job) (up{cluster="$cluster",namespace=~"capi-system|capi-kubeadm-bootstrap-system|capi-kubeadm-control-plane-system|capo-system|orc-system"} == 1) unless on (job) (max by (job) (leader_election_master_status{cluster="$cluster",namespace=~"capi-system|capi-kubeadm-bootstrap-system|capi-kubeadm-control-plane-system|capo-system|orc-system"}) == 1)) or vector(0)

panels.title: CAPO OpenStack API error ratio
panels.description: Share of OpenStack API calls made by CAPO that returned an error, over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Reconcile errors (range)
panels.description: Reconcile errors across CAPI, CAPO and ORC controllers over the dashboard time range. Some errors are normal (for example waiting on OpenStack); a sustained rate is not.

panels.title: Reconcile panics (range)
panels.description: Reconcile panics across CAPI, CAPO and ORC controllers. Any value is a bug worth raising upstream.

panels.title: Controller pod restarts (range)
panels.description: Container restarts in the CAPI, CAPO, ORC and addon-provider namespaces over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Cluster summary
panels.description: One row per workload cluster. CP = KubeadmControlPlane. Ready below desired, or up-to-date below desired, means a scale or rollout is in progress or stuck. The namespace is magnum-<OpenStack project ID>.

panels.title: Cluster conditions
panels.description: Cluster API v1beta2 conditions per cluster. Health conditions (Available, InfrastructureReady and so on) should be True. Activity conditions (RollingOut, ScalingUp, ScalingDown, Remediating, Deleting, Paused) are normally False and show True while that activity is under way. InfrastructureReady comes from the OpenStackCluster (CAPO).

panels.title: Cluster phase
panels.description: Cluster API Cluster phase over time.

targets.expr: sum by (name) (capi_cluster_status_phase{cluster="$cluster",name=~"$wl"} * on (phase) group_left () (label_replace(vector(1), "phase", "Pending", "", "") or label_replace(vector(2), "phase", "Provisioning", "", "") or label_replace(vector(3), "phase", "Provisioned", "", "") or label_replace(vector(4), "phase", "Deleting", "", "") or label_replace(vector(5), "phase", "Failed", "", "") or label_replace(vector(6), "phase", "Unknown", "", "")))

panels.title: Cluster Available condition
panels.description: The v1beta2 Available condition over time. This rolls up infrastructure, control plane, workers and the remote connection probe.

panels.title: Cluster cache connection
panels.description: Whether the CAPI controllers can reach each workload cluster's API server (minimum across the core, bootstrap and control-plane controllers). A disconnect blocks node reference, drain and health checks.

panels.title: Cluster cache health check failures
panels.description: Failed health checks from the management cluster to each workload cluster API server, summed across controllers. Repeated failures lead to a cache disconnect.

panels.title: Machines by phase
panels.description: Current count of Machines in each phase for the selected workload clusters.

panels.title: Machines by phase over time
panels.description: Machine count per phase over time. Provisioning or Deleting that lingers points at CAPO or OpenStack.

panels.title: Machines not Running
panels.description: Machines currently in any phase other than Running.

panels.title: Machine phase
panels.description: Phase of every Machine over time. Replaced Machines appear as new rows (rollouts, remediation, autoscaling).

targets.expr: sum by (name) (capi_machine_status_phase{cluster="$cluster",cluster_name=~"$wl"} * on (phase) group_left () (label_replace(vector(1), "phase", "Pending", "", "") or label_replace(vector(2), "phase", "Provisioning", "", "") or label_replace(vector(3), "phase", "Provisioned", "", "") or label_replace(vector(4), "phase", "Running", "", "") or label_replace(vector(5), "phase", "Deleting", "", "") or label_replace(vector(6), "phase", "Deleted", "", "") or label_replace(vector(7), "phase", "Failed", "", "") or label_replace(vector(8), "phase", "Unknown", "", "")))

panels.title: Control plane replicas short
panels.description: KubeadmControlPlane desired replicas minus ready, and minus up-to-date. Zero is healthy. A non-zero 'not up-to-date' that persists means a control plane rollout (for example a Kubernetes upgrade) is stuck.

panels.title: Worker replicas short
panels.description: MachineDeployment desired replicas minus ready, and minus available. Short-lived bumps are normal when the autoscaler adds nodes; a sustained gap means workers are failing to join.

panels.title: Worker pool size
panels.description: Desired and ready worker replicas per cluster. Desired changes over time are the magnum cluster-autoscaler (one per cluster, in the magnum-* namespaces) or a user resize.

panels.title: MachineDeployments
panels.description: Current state of each worker pool (MachineDeployment).

panels.title: OpenStack API request rate by call
panels.description: OpenStack API calls made by capo-controller-manager, by call type (for example server_get, port_list). Rate rises with the number of clusters and with reconcile retries. Uses a rolling 30 minute window because CAPO calls OpenStack in bursts.

panels.title: OpenStack API errors by call
panels.description: OpenStack API calls from CAPO that returned an error. Correlate with nova, neutron, octavia and keystone logs via nectar-logs. Uses a rolling 30 minute window because CAPO calls OpenStack in bursts.

panels.title: OpenStack API latency p95 by call
panels.description: 95th percentile OpenStack API call latency as seen by CAPO. The histogram tops out at 10s. Uses a rolling 30 minute window because CAPO calls OpenStack in bursts.

panels.title: OpenStack API latency (all calls)
panels.description: Overall CAPO OpenStack API latency percentiles. Uses a rolling 30 minute window because CAPO calls OpenStack in bursts.

panels.title: OpenStack API calls over range
panels.description: Per-call totals over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: CAPO reconcile errors by controller
panels.description: Reconcile errors in CAPO controllers (openstackcluster, openstackmachine, openstackserver, openstackfloatingippool). Find the cause in the capo-controller-manager logs.

panels.title: CAPO reconcile rate by result
panels.description: CAPO reconcile outcomes. A high 'requeue_after' share is normal while waiting on OpenStack (for example a server building).

panels.title: CAPO reconcile duration p95 by controller
panels.description: 95th percentile reconcile time for CAPO controllers. Mostly OpenStack API latency, since each reconcile makes several API calls. Uses a rolling 30 minute window because CAPO calls OpenStack in bursts.

panels.title: Scrape target up
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape each controller's metrics endpoint.

panels.title: Leader election
panels.description: Pod holding each controller's leader lease. Each deployment runs one replica, so a missing row means the controller is down.

panels.title: Reconcile rate by result
panels.description: Reconcile outcomes per controller manager.

panels.title: Reconcile errors by controller
panels.description: Reconcile errors per controller. Errors are retried with backoff, so check whether they persist.

panels.title: Reconcile duration p99 by controller
panels.description: 99th percentile reconcile time per controller.

panels.title: Terminal errors, timeouts and panics
panels.description: Terminal errors are not retried, so the object stays broken until someone intervenes. Panics are controller bugs.

panels.title: Workqueue depth
panels.description: Items waiting to be reconciled. Sustained depth means the controller cannot keep up.

panels.title: Workqueue wait p99
panels.description: How long items wait in the queue before a worker picks them up. Compare with worker saturation.

panels.title: Longest running reconcile
panels.description: Age of the oldest reconcile still running per queue. A value that climbs steadily means a reconcile is hung (for example blocked on an unresponsive OpenStack or workload cluster API).

panels.title: Worker saturation
panels.description: Active reconcile workers as a share of the controller's concurrency limit. Sustained 100% means the --*-concurrency flag is the bottleneck.

targets.expr: sum by (job, controller) (controller_runtime_active_workers{cluster="$cluster",job=~"$job"}) / sum by (job, controller) (controller_runtime_max_concurrent_reconciles{cluster="$cluster",job=~"$job"}) > 0

panels.title: Workqueue retries
panels.description: Items re-queued with rate-limited backoff, usually after an error.

panels.title: Webhook requests by code
panels.description: Admission and conversion webhook calls served by the controllers. Code 500 means the API server rejected a create or update because the webhook failed.

panels.title: Webhook latency p99
panels.description: 99th percentile webhook latency. Slow webhooks slow every create and update of CAPI objects.

panels.title: Management API server client requests
panels.description: Requests from the controllers to the management cluster's kube-apiserver, by HTTP code. 429 means client-side or API priority and fairness throttling; <error> means the request never got a response.

panels.title: CPU usage by pod
panels.description: CPU used by CAPI, CAPO, ORC and addon-provider pods.

panels.title: Memory working set by pod
panels.description: Memory working set of CAPI, CAPO, ORC and addon-provider pods. Controller memory grows with the number of objects they cache.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: Container restarts per pod.

panels.title: Restarts and last termination
panels.description: Lifetime restart count per pod and why the container last terminated (from kube-state-metrics). Use 'nectar-kubectl --cluster <cluster> logs --previous' (add --env test for test-capi) for the crashed container's logs.
